Getting started

  1. Click the link above. You will need to be signed in to a free Google account.
  2. Google will ask if you want to make a copy. Say yes — that copy is yours, saved in your own Google Drive, and nothing you type is visible to anyone else.
  3. On the Candle tab, set Weigh in to grams or ounces.
  4. Enter the water weight of your jar. Everything else follows from it.
How to weigh your jar. Put the empty jar on your scale and zero it. Fill it with water up to the height you want the wax to reach, leaving room for the lid. That water weight is the number the whole sheet starts from.

The three tabs

  • Candle — your jar and your fragrance. Wax and oil, per candle and per batch.
  • Costs & Price — what it costs you, and what to charge.
  • Reference — every assumption, where to change it, and what each box means.

Two things worth knowing

Fragrance load and fragrance content are different numbers. 20 g of fragrance in 200 g of wax is a 10% load — but 9.09% content. Same candle. Pick whichever your recipe or your wax sheet uses; the calculator shows you both either way.
Adding 40% to your cost does not give you a 40% margin. It gives you about 29%. The sheet works out the price that actually delivers the margin you asked for, once your selling fees come out.
This calculator does not choose your wick. Nothing can. Wick size depends on your wax, your fragrance load, your dye and the shape of your jar — the only way to know is to burn a test candle and watch the melt pool. Use the printable Burn Test Log that came with this download to keep track of what you try.

Colours in the sheet

  • Cream boxes — type in these.
  • Grey boxes — these work themselves out. Don't type over them.
  • Blue boxes — starting assumptions you can change whenever you like.

If something is not right

Message me through Etsy and I will help. If a number looks wrong, tell me what you entered and what you expected — that is usually enough to sort it out quickly.
